cards.raw0: The normal neonatal thymus appears "{{c1::sail}}-shaped" on a chest X-ray
cards.back: This will then involute with age [img] Photo credit: Nevit Dilmen , CC BY-SA 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons, Hilarmont , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons; the supplementary image with overlays of the relevant areas was adapted from the image mentioned previously, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0

cards.front: What is the most common intra-abdominal organ injured during blunt trauma? [Spleen]
cards.raw0:
What is the most common intra-abdominal organ injured during blunt trauma?

{{c1::Spleen}}
cards.back: Splenic lacerations can result in hemorrhage and phrenic nerve irritation (shoulder pain, hiccups) [img] Photo credit: ChocChocsugarsugar , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: Edema may be caused by [lymphatic] disruption/obstruction
cards.raw0: Edema may be caused by {{c1::lymphatic}} disruption/obstruction
cards.back: - Impaired removal of excess interstitial fluid leads to swelling & pain - Starts as pitting edema → progresses to nonpitting edema + firm, thickened skin - Etiologies include malignancy , iatrogenic causes (lymph node dissection & radiation), chronic inflammation (recurrent cellulitis), and severe venous insufficiency ; obesity is also contributing factor - Classic (but less common) cause is filariasis [img] Photo credit: DocHealer , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: Splenic lacerations can irritate the [phrenic] nerve
cards.raw0: Splenic lacerations can irritate the {{c1::phrenic}} nerve
cards.back: - This is because the spleen is right underneath the left diaphragm - Splenic lacerations can irritate the sensory fibers around the diaphragm, leading to shoulder pain ( Kehr sign ) and hiccups (spasmodic diaphragm contraction pulling air against a closed larynx) [img] Splenic rupture is seen in the bottom right of the CT Photo credit: Hellerhoff , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: Does the medial tract of the superficial lymphatic system of the lower extremity bypass the popliteal nodes ? [Yes]
cards.raw0:
Does the medial tract of the superficial lymphatic system of the lower extremity bypass the popliteal nodes?

{{c1::Yes}}
cards.back: - Thus lesions on the medial foot cause inguinal lymphadenopathy only - L ateral L ymphatics take a L onger route [img]

cards.front: Does the lateral tract of the superficial lymphatic system of the lower extremity bypass the popliteal nodes? [No]
cards.raw0:
Does the lateral tract of the superficial lymphatic system of the lower extremity bypass the popliteal nodes?

{{c1::No}}
cards.back: - Thus, lesions on the lateral foot are more likely to cause lymphadenopathy in the popliteal and inguinal areas - L ateral L ymphatics take a L onger route [img]

cards.front: What lymph node cluster drains the apex of the tongue , floor of the mouth, and lower lip? [Submental lymph nodes]
cards.raw0:
What lymph node cluster drains the apex of the tongue, floor of the mouth, and lower lip?

{{c1::Submental lymph nodes}}
cards.back: - Thus, a tumor on the apex of the tongue would drain here - AKA cervical lymph node level 1A [img] Photo credit: Mikael Häggström, M.D , CC0, via Wikimedia Commons [img]

cards.front: What lymph node cluster drains the cheeks , gums , anterior tongue , anterior nasal cavity , and soft tissue of the midface ? [Submandibular lymph nodes]
cards.raw0:
What lymph node cluster drains the cheeks, gums, anterior tongue, anterior nasal cavity, and soft tissue of the midface?

{{c1::Submandibular lymph nodes}}
cards.back: Also drain the submandibular gland; this is also known as cervical lymph node level 1B [img] Photo credit: Mikael Häggström, M.D , CC0, via Wikimedia Commons [img]

cards.front: What lymph node cluster drains the nasal cavity, nasopharynx, and auditory tubes? [Retropharyngeal lymph nodes]
cards.raw0:
What lymph node cluster drains the nasal cavity, nasopharynx, and auditory tubes?

{{c1::Retropharyngeal lymph nodes}}
cards.back: - These are located in the retropharyngeal space (space between the buccopharyngeal fascia and the prevertebral fascia) and frequently disappear by age 4-5 - Thus retropharyngeal abscess is rare in older children (and is considered largely a disease of children) [img]

cards.front: What lymph node cluster drains the oropharynx , hypopharynx , nasopharynx ? [Upper jugular chain nodes]
cards.raw0:
What lymph node cluster drains the oropharynx, hypopharynx, nasopharynx?

{{c1::Upper jugular chain nodes}}
cards.back: - Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas typically drain here; these are located by internal jugular vein - This is also known as cervical lymph node level 2 [img] Photo credit: Mikael Häggström, M.D. , CC0, via Wikimedia Commons [img] Photo credit: OpenStax , CC BY 4.0 [img]

cards.front: Basophilic RBC nuclear remnants [Howell-Jolly bodies] [img]
cards.raw0:
Basophilic RBC nuclear remnants

{{c1::Howell-Jolly bodies}}
cards.back: Photo credit: Paulo Henrique Orlandi Mourao and Mikael Häggström , CC BY-SA 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons Due to splenectomy or a nonfunctional spleen (e.g., sickle cell disease ) → inability to remove nuclear remnants of RBCs [img]

cards.front: Basophilic remnants of DNA within RBC nuclei (1st) = [Asplenia (Howell-Jolly bodies)] Precipitation of ribosomal RNA within RBC cytoplasm (2nd) = [Lead poisoning (basophilic stippling)] [img] [img]
cards.raw0:
Basophilic remnants of DNA within RBC nuclei (1st) = {{c1::Asplenia (Howell-Jolly bodies)::Histologic finding and cause}}
Precipitation of ribosomal RNA within RBC cytoplasm (2nd) = {{c1::Lead poisoning (basophilic stippling)::Histologic finding and cause}}
cards.back: Photo credit: Paulo Henrique, et al , CC BY-SA 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons & Mikael Häggström, M.D , CC0, via Wikimedia Commons - The spleen usually removes Howell-Jolly bodies (one nucleus = one dot). May also be seen in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or megaloblastic anemia - Basophilic stippling is due to aggregation of ribosomes. Non-specific; may also see with sideroblastic anemia and thalassemia - Nuclear vs. cytoplasmic inclusion bodies (both basophilic) [img]

cards.front: Naive B-cells migrate to [ secondary ] lymphoid organs
cards.raw0: Naive B-cells migrate to {{c1::secondary}} lymphoid organs
cards.back: - Immature B cells leave bone marrow and migrate to the spleen white pulp to mature (i.e., become naive B cells) - Naive B cells (i.e., mature but haven't encountered an antigen before) move to these organs to complete maturation [img]

cards.front: Which region of the lymph node enlarges and multiplies during humoral immune response (e.g., bacterial infection)? [Germinal centers]
cards.raw0:
Which region of the lymph node enlarges and multiplies during humoral immune response (e.g., bacterial infection)?

{{c1::Germinal centers}}
cards.back: Increased number of germinal centers → lymphadenopathy [img]
